title: Complete Absence of Authentication Logging
evidence: api/auth.py imports logger but never uses it. No logs for successful or failed logins.
risk: Brute force attacks or unauthorized access attempts are invisible to operators. No audit trail for password changes.
recommended_fix: Add logger.info for successful logins and logger.warning for failed attempts (redacting passwords).

title: User Management Actions are Not Logged
evidence: api/users.py and user_service.py have zero log statements. Admin actions on users are silent.
risk: Malicious or accidental account deletions/suspensions cannot be traced to a specific administrator action.
recommended_fix: Log actor ID, target ID, and action (approve/suspend/delete) in both the router and service layer.

title: Secrets Access and Deletion are Not Logged
evidence: Upsert is logged, but listing all secrets (sensitive) and deleting them is silent.
risk: Unauthorized viewing of secret metadata or sabotage via secret deletion goes undetected.
recommended_fix: Add logs for all secrets endpoints, especially list and delete.

title: Logs Lack User Correlation
evidence: The log buffer captures job_id and character_id but explicitly omits user_id and request_id.
risk: Logs cannot be correlated to specific users, making it impossible to audit which user triggered which job or mutation.
recommended_fix: Update BackendLogRecord and middleware to include user_id and request_id.

title: Minimal Frontend UI Action Traceability
evidence: Only API errors are emitted to logBus. Success actions (e.g. 'user clicked create') are mostly silent in the browser bus.
risk: Debugging complex UI flows is difficult when only terminal errors are logged.
recommended_fix: Add informational logBus.emit calls for major user navigation and form submissions.

title: System Logs Access is Not Logged
evidence: The endpoint skips itself in the request logger and has no internal logger call. Accessing all system logs is silent.
risk: If an admin account is compromised, the attacker can read all logs to gain further intel without leaving a trace in the logs themselves.
recommended_fix: Log the administrator actor who accessed the system logs snapshot.
